cells.tense: Right now you're putting a piece of what you see in front of other people, and it's holding.
cells.ask: Draw it once from memory, without checking, and hand it to someone who needs the road.
cells.core:
You can hold a pattern clear of its details, and something in you wants to put it where other people can use it. The shape shows to you plain, and then you draw it. That's the amount to be working at.

When the drawing is steady like this, the care underneath it is legible. Nothing is forced. What the work asks to keep teaching is feeding something specific: structure emerging at the base, skilled work building something new. That's what this is free to feed next, and it's optional by definition.

You can tell the pattern is real to you because not being sure of every detail doesn't stall the hand. Reach around those. Hand this over while it's live.

cells.tense: You're not guiding from where the pattern shows yet; you're guiding from a version of what comes after it lands.
cells.ask: Make one clear direction and wait for its result before adjusting anything.
cells.core:
You're handed a clear idea — the shape of a thing with its details stripped — and instead of putting it in front of anyone you're working out how it will land. Who will misunderstand it, which version will answer that, what you'll say when they do. You've been running that before anything reaches a page.

You've got a lot of the shape, and not much of it is written where it can be argued with. Pushing it out like this costs you the actual exchange, which is the thing you know how to navigate.

Practice flows without force when it settles — working alone connects rather than cuts off. For now, one direction, and then stop to see what happened.

cells.tense: There's a clear shape you stopped drawing, and it hasn't gone out since.
cells.ask: Name what's fair in one exchange you've been part of this week.
cells.core:
The pattern's there. The hand stopped. What's noted is the not-going-out, not the shape itself. So the shape stays private, and day to day it's mostly you not saying what you'd draw. Nothing much is coming through your pen.

Working the shape out alone connects you to people instead of cutting you off, and the careful seeing serves the work rather than feeding worry. That part is still available to you today, and you can tell because the drawing never needed an audience to be real — it only needed to leave the page. What's running low here is the felt sense of what's owed and what's fair. That's where the supply comes from, not from forcing work into the starved part. Small trade, real information, then back to drawing what you see.

cells.tense: You're already drawing the route when you talk, and calling it just the shape of the situation.
cells.ask: Say 'this is mine' about one clear direction you've been calling the natural way things go.
cells.core:
You're laying structure in front of people all the time — your order, your emphasis, what you leave out — and the whole time it reads to you as just the shape. The hand is moving. The credit isn't.

It shows most with your own projects: decisions you've already made get described as if they came out of nowhere, which is a smaller story than what's actually happening. The connection underneath that matters is getting missed in the same way — the decisive join of two streams, which shows up precisely when you stop pretending everything arrived on its own.

Small and plain, then let it run a moment before you explain it away.
